correctness.rationale: For stars, a color class has size at most floor((n-1)/2) unless K_1,1; n=2 is impossible. With two colors on m,n>=2, parity of m+n-2 and the identity row_i+col_j=H+2*x_ij force one whole side constant, hence m=2 and n even. Three-color cyclic i+j mod 3 satisfies local caps except (3,4),(4,4),(4,5),(4,7); explicit 4x4 and 4x7 matrices independently passed. For K_3,4, every valid color class of four edges is a C4 (18 cases), so partition into three four-cycles would force every vertex degree even, impossible. For K_4,5, each color class has at most six edges; 3 colors cover at most 18<20. Four-color modular constructions work. General inequalities prove infinite ranges. Independent 2^12/2^20 local-subgraph enumeration found maxima four and six; finite tests do not establish unbounded claims.
